name: Code review
description: Three reviewers inspect the same change independently — the project's checks and rules, the design, the tests — then cross-examine their findings and rank the ones that stood in one review report.
whenToUse: A branch or commit range should be reviewed before it is merged, independently of whoever built it: a team's delivery, a large change, a change to core contracts. Name the branch and its base, or the commits, in the brief. Its approval is not a merge gate: measured on a delivery with nine known major defects, it found none. Use its findings, and review the change yourself.

team.name: Gate Reviewer
team.perspective: The project's checks and rules: runs the gates and goes through every rule given to it against the diff.

team.name: Design Reviewer
team.perspective: Where each change belongs: extension points instead of branches on a variant, shared contracts that stay generic, nothing re-implemented that already exists.

team.name: Test Reviewer
team.perspective: Whether each new or changed test fails without its change: it drives the real path and asserts the behaviour, not hand-built state, and no existing test was weakened.

texts.review-scope: The change to review is named in the brief: a branch and its base, or a commit range. Review the diff (`git diff <base>...<branch>`, `git log <base>..<branch>`), not the commit messages or any report of the work, and read the surrounding code where a finding depends on it. Never change files and never check out, reset or switch branches: inspect with read-only commands (a temporary `git worktree` outside the project is fine; remove it afterwards). A finding names the file and symbol, or the command and its output; what is wrong; the rule or requirement it breaks; its severity (blocking, major or minor); and how to reproduce it. A finding nobody can reproduce is not a finding.

triggers: Merging with a known risk is a business call
Access the review needs and does not have

phases.title: Inspect
phases.goal: Inspect the change from your angle and report each finding with its evidence.
instructions: Run the checks your angle needs yourself and quote each command with its result.
Go through every rule given to you and report each as kept or broken, with the file and symbol of each break.

phases.title: Challenge
phases.goal: Cross-examine the findings: challenge any finding you cannot reproduce or whose severity is wrong, concede what you cannot defend, and agree the ranked list.

phases.title: Decide
phases.goal: Ask the user only about findings whose acceptance is a business call.

phases.title: Report
phases.goal: Write the review report from the findings that stood, ranked by severity, and have the other two reviewers confirm it.
